title: Elo through 1.0.0 permits code injection through source strings and programmatic ASTs
summary: Elo has three independent injection flaws: JavaScript constructor access can execute host code, Ruby interpolation can execute commands, and unchecked AST fields can inject generated JavaScript, Ruby, Python or SQL.

severity.rationale: Attacker-supplied Elo source can execute code through documented CLI and library paths. CI and agent pipelines that evaluate untrusted expressions expose the host runtime.

affected.note: All three advisories list versions through 1.0.0.

exposure: Requires processing attacker-controlled Elo source or programmatic ASTs. Ruby injection requires executing the Ruby output; AST injection requires attacker-influenced node fields.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 1.0.1 before evaluating untrusted Elo input.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm the installed version or revision and exercise the affected workflow with trusted inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
